clusters.label: Thermodynamic stability
clusters.definition: Thermodynamic favorability of a material phase under the stated conditions.
clusters.reason: All denote the same thermodynamic property. Materials, assessment methods, conditions and the explicitly negated assertion remain claim-specific; supporting mechanical or phonon analyses are not themselves merged with this property.

clusters.label: Anharmonicity
clusters.definition: Departure of lattice vibrations from harmonic behavior.
clusters.reason: The supplied passages describe lattice anharmonicity across materials. Alloying, structural distortion and bond chemistry are distinct proposed origins of the same property; the last mention does not specifically restrict its referent to quartic anharmonicity.

clusters.label: Material degradation
clusters.definition: Deterioration of a material during thermoelectric operation under electrical and thermal stress.
clusters.reason: Both denote operational material deterioration associated with mobile species. Electromigration, Cu precipitation and unsuccessful mitigation remain separate claim details.

clusters.label: Electrochemical Seebeck coefficient alpha = dV/dT
clusters.definition: Temperature derivative of electrode potential for the Fe2+/Fe3+ redox system in organic solvents.
clusters.reason: Both explicitly concern the same redox electrochemical thermopower; solvent, concentration, coordination and viscosity dependencies remain attached to their claims.

clusters.label: Quasi-one-dimensional structure
clusters.definition: A crystal structural class characterized by extended chains with predominantly one-dimensional connectivity.
clusters.reason: Both labels denote the dimensional structural class supported by tetrahedral chains. Their compositions, chain bonding and crystallographic details remain distinct.

clusters.label: Coexisting ionic and covalent bonds
clusters.definition: Presence of both ionic and covalent bonding within a material structure.
clusters.reason: Both passages explicitly describe coexistence of these bonding types. The Zintl-like interpretation applies only to the Cs2[PdCl4]I2 claim.

clusters.label: High Seebeck coefficients
clusters.definition: Large electronic thermopower in the supplied computational thermoelectric analyses.
clusters.reason: All describe high electronic Seebeck coefficients, with no explicit conflicting sign or transport subtype. Band mechanisms and material conditions remain claim-specific.

clusters.label: Enhanced electronic conductivity
clusters.definition: Increased electronic electrical conductivity in MIL/SWCNT composite films.
clusters.reason: The paper title identifies electron conductivity, and the evidence associates its enhancement with interfacial interactions.

unresolved.reason: Na+/Cl− shielding is linked to enhanced hydrogel conductivity, but the supplied evidence does not identify its charge-transport type sufficiently to establish equivalence with electronic conductivity.

clusters.label: High ZT
clusters.definition: Reported high dimensionless thermoelectric figure of merit of superionic Ag8SnSe6.
clusters.reason: The evidence reports high ZT for Ag8SnSe6 without identifying it as a first-principles prediction or specifying the evaluation method.

clusters.label: High zT (first-principles prediction)
clusters.definition: High dimensionless thermoelectric figure of merit predicted for two-dimensional Nb2XSe2 materials.
clusters.reason: Explicitly derived from first-principles and Boltzmann transport calculations; kept separate from the report with unspecified evaluation method.

clusters.label: ZT approximately 1.1
clusters.definition: A dimensionless thermoelectric figure of merit of approximately 1.1.
clusters.reason: Both denote the same quantity and approximate value. Different compositions, mechanisms and the stated 450 °C condition remain attached to their respective claims.

clusters.label: Ferromagnetic state

clusters.reason: All explicitly identify ferromagnetic ordering in computational studies. Dopants, compositions, magnetic moments and relative stability are claim-specific.
